identification.summary: China-based espionage actor that Microsoft tracks as Heart Typhoon and that Mandiant/Google tracks as APT17 [S1][S2]. FireEye reported that APT17 had conducted network intrusions against the U.S. government, international law firms and information technology companies, and that it had used the BLACKCOFFEE malware since 2013 [S3]. In 2014-2015 the group hid encoded command-and-control (C2) addresses in Microsoft TechNet forum profiles and posts [S3]. In 2024 Italian firm TG Soft attributed spear-phishing campaigns against Italian companies and government entities, using a 9002 RAT variant, to APT17 [S9].
identification.firstObserved: The Hacker News says Mandiant (then FireEye) first documented APT17 in 2013 [S9]. FireEye says APT17 had used BLACKCOFFEE since 2013 [S3]. Symantec dates the related Hidden Lynx cluster to 2009 and links it to Operation Aurora (2009-2010) [S5][S6].
identification.notes: Microsoft lists HELIUM, AURORA PANDA, APT17, Hidden Lynx, ATG3, Red Typhoon, KAOS, TG-8153, SportsFans, DeputyDog and Tailgater as other names for Heart Typhoon [S1]. MITRE tracks the group as APT17 (G0025) [S2]. FireEye states that APT17 is also known as Deputy Dog [S3]. Symantec's Hidden Lynx is a broader cluster (an estimated 50-100 operators in two teams) that Symantec did not equate with APT17 in the sources reviewed here, so Hidden Lynx facts are kept separate below [S5][S6].

attribution.sponsor: People's Republic of China (assessed). FireEye calls APT17 a China-based threat group [S3]. In July 2019 the anonymous research group Intrusion Truth alleged that APT17 is run by the Jinan bureau of the Ministry of State Security (MSS) through contractors managed by alleged MSS officer Guo Lin [S7][S8].
attribution.confidence: FireEye 'assesses' that APT17 was behind the TechNet activity but gives no formal confidence level [S3]. The MSS Jinan link rests on Intrusion Truth's allegations, which press coverage and CERT-EU treat as unverified claims [S7][S8]. No U.S. government indictment or advisory naming APT17 was found in this research.
attribution.basis: Vendor technical reporting (FireEye/Microsoft joint TechNet investigation) [S3]; Intrusion Truth open-source identity research covering Guo Lin, Wang Qingwei and Zeng Xiaoyong, and Jinan front companies, plus code similarities to the ZoxRPC malware [S7][S8]; Microsoft and MITRE name mappings [S1][S2].

objectives: Cyber-espionage against government, defense, legal and technology targets [S2][S3]. CFR reports that APT17 also targeted Chinese citizens for financial gain [S10]. Symantec assessed the related Hidden Lynx cluster as a hacker-for-hire operation that collects information for clients, while CrowdStrike's Dmitri Alperovitch argued it was closely tied to the Chinese government [S5].

sectors: Security vendors (Bit9, via the Hidden Lynx cluster)
regions: Global; 52 percent of Hidden Lynx targets were in the U.S. [S5]
targeting.notes: U.S. government, defense, law, IT, mining and NGO targeting is from MITRE [S2] and FireEye [S3]. Japanese media, manufacturing and government targeting is from FireEye's 2013 DeputyDog reporting, as covered by the press [S4]. Italian corporate and government targeting is from TG Soft, as covered by the press [S9]. Hidden Lynx figures apply to Symantec's broader cluster [S5].

capabilities.summary: Uses legitimate public sites as dead-drop resolvers: BLACKCOFFEE retrieved encoded C2 IPs that had been posted to TechNet profiles and forums [S3]. Used strategic web compromise (watering holes) with an Internet Explorer zero-day (CVE-2013-3893) in the 2013 DeputyDog campaign [S4]. In 2024 used spear-phishing with Office documents and links to a fake Skype for Business MSI hosted on a domain that imitated an Italian government site; the chain ran a VBS script and a Java archive that decrypted 9002 RAT shellcode [S9]. TG Soft describes 9002 RAT as modular, with traffic monitoring, screenshots, file enumeration, process management, command execution and diskless variants [S9]. In the related Hidden Lynx cluster, Symantec describes code-signing abuse after the Bit9 breach, plus the Moudoor and Naid trojans [S5][S6]. MITRE lists BLACKCOFFEE as APT17 software [S2].

campaigns.name: Operation Aurora (Hidden Lynx linkage)
campaigns.summary: Symantec links the Hidden Lynx cluster to Operation Aurora: the Naid trojan was used there, and Symantec says the group either carried out the attack or worked with the attackers [S5][S6]. The Hacker News notes that 9002 RAT (Hydraq/McRAT) was the tool used in Aurora [S9].

campaigns.name: VOHO watering hole / Bit9 compromise (Hidden Lynx)
campaigns.summary: According to Symantec as reported by the press, Hidden Lynx breached security firm Bit9 and signed malware with Bit9 keys after Bit9 software blocked attacks on U.S. defense contractors; Bit9 disclosed the breach in February 2013. The VOHO watering-hole campaign compromised about 4,000 machines [S5][S6].

campaigns.name: Operation DeputyDog
campaigns.summary: Starting 19 August 2013, watering-hole attacks compromised at least three major Japanese media sites and served an IE zero-day (CVE-2013-3893) against manufacturing, government and media targets. FireEye linked the actor to the Bit9 compromise through a shared IP address [S4].

campaigns.name: TechNet C2 obfuscation
campaigns.summary: FireEye and Microsoft found that a BLACKCOFFEE variant retrieved encoded C2 IPs from TechNet profiles and forum posts. They sinkholed the activity by encoding a sinkhole IP into the posts, and released IOCs and signatures in May 2015 [S3][S10].

campaigns.name: Intrusion Truth exposure
campaigns.summary: Intrusion Truth alleged that APT17 is run by the MSS Jinan bureau and named Guo Lin, Wang Qingwei and Zeng Xiaoyong [S7][S8].

campaigns.name: Italian 9002 RAT campaign
campaigns.summary: On 24 June and 2 July 2024, spear-phishing delivered a fake Skype for Business package that dropped a 9002 RAT variant on Italian companies and government entities; TG Soft attributed the activity to APT17 [S9].

diamond.adversary: PRC-based operators tracked as Heart Typhoon/APT17 [S1][S3]. Intrusion Truth alleges MSS Jinan bureau management through Jinan front companies [S7][S8].
diamond.capability: BLACKCOFFEE [S2][S3]; 9002 RAT variant [S9]; IE zero-day CVE-2013-3893 [S4]; Moudoor/Naid and stolen code-signing keys in the related Hidden Lynx cluster [S5][S6].
diamond.infrastructure: Legitimate public sites (TechNet) used as dead-drop resolvers for C2 [S3]; compromised Japanese media sites as watering holes and a Hong Kong payload host [S4]; a look-alike Italian government domain [S9].
diamond.victim: U.S. government, defense, law and IT organizations [S2][S3]; Japanese media, manufacturing and government organizations [S4]; Italian companies and government entities [S9].
diamond.socioPolitical: Intelligence collection that serves PRC interests; Intrusion Truth alleges MSS tasking [S7][S8]. Symantec's hacker-for-hire framing of Hidden Lynx is disputed [S5].
diamond.technology: Windows endpoints and Internet Explorer [S4]; user trust in collaboration software (Skype for Business) [S9]; web forums used for C2 resolution [S3].

gaps: No Microsoft Threat Intelligence publication describing activity under the Heart Typhoon name was found; the Microsoft name rests on Microsoft's naming mapping [S1]. learn.microsoft.com could not be fetched.
The Hidden Lynx/APT17 relationship is asserted by Microsoft's alias list [S1] but is not detailed in the sources reviewed; Symantec's cluster is broader and may include other actors.
Intrusion Truth's MSS Jinan attribution is unverified, and no U.S. government indictment, sanction or advisory naming APT17 was found.
The primary reports could not be opened: TG Soft (2024), Symantec's Hidden Lynx white paper, FireEye's DeputyDog blog, and Intrusion Truth's posts. Their details rely on secondary coverage.
Activity after 2024 and current infrastructure are unknown.

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. STEP 1: Key terrain includes widely visited public websites (news, forum and government look-alike domains) that can serve as watering holes or dead-drop resolvers, and user endpoints at government, defense, legal and IT organizations [S2][S3][S4][S9]. STEP 2: C2 hidden in legitimate sites blends with normal traffic and weakens IP blocklists [S3]. STEP 3: Observed templates are a watering hole with a browser zero-day leading to a RAT [S4], and spear-phishing with a fake software installer leading to MSI, VBS, JAR and in-memory 9002 RAT [S9]. STEP 4: MLCOA is spear-phishing with trusted-software lures against government and defense-adjacent organizations to deploy modular RATs for espionage [S9]. MDCOA is a supply-chain or code-signing compromise of a security or IT vendor, as in the Hidden Lynx Bit9 case, to deliver trusted-signed malware into defense networks [S5][S6]. Candidate indicators: endpoints fetching forum or profile pages and then contacting unrelated IPs; MSI installers that spawn wscript and java; unsigned 'Skype for Business' packages from non-Microsoft domains [S3][S9].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. Situational awareness: correlate dead-drop-resolver patterns and look-alike government domains across DODIN and partner feeds [S3][S9]. Authorities: the TechNet sinkhole was a private-sector (FireEye/Microsoft) action [S3], so disruption of public-platform abuse likely depends on coordination with platform owners rather than military action alone. Mission assurance: prioritize monitoring and patch speed on defense-contractor and legal-support enclaves that hold program data [S2][S3]. Coordination: the actor's victims span allied nations (Japan, Italy) [S4][S9], which supports sharing indicators with partner CERTs; attribution to the MSS remains unofficial [S7].
